run_dispersion.criteria: fit {coefficients, alpha, diff_shrink, home_field_runs_adj} on the fit half of a 70% date split; on the HELD-OUT half all four must hold: (1) home win, paired Brier, non-inferiority, one-sided 95% lower bound on delta >= -0.001; (2) THE RUNLINE, BOTH SIDES, scored as the per-game SUM of the log loss on home margin >= 2 and the log loss on home margin <= -2 (equivalently home -1.5 and away -1.5; the +1.5 sides are their complements and score identically), paired, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (3) total over 9.0, paired log loss, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (4) runs both sides, out-of-sample log-likelihood per row, NB > Poisson. Moneyline is non-inferiority because diff_shrink already absorbs its calibration and NB must not be credited for beating it there. AMENDED 2026-08-09: V1 said only 'margin >= 2' and did not name a side, the first run scored the home side alone, and the side changes the verdict; see RUNLINE_SIDE_AMENDMENT. The verdict is taken from `dispersion_gate_sensitivity`, which requires the amended criterion to hold at split quantiles 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, not from any single split.
run_dispersion.criteria_v1: fit {coefficients, alpha, diff_shrink, home_field_runs_adj} on the fit half of a 70% date split; on the HELD-OUT half all four must hold: (1) home win, paired Brier, non-inferiority, one-sided 95% lower bound on delta >= -0.001; (2) margin >= 2, paired log loss, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (3) total over 9.0, paired log loss, delta > 0 at t >= 1.645; (4) runs both sides, out-of-sample log-likelihood per row, NB > Poisson. Moneyline is non-inferiority because diff_shrink already absorbs its calibration and NB must not be credited for beating it there.

checks.criterion: runline (both sides, per-game sum of the two log losses), paired log loss, superiority
runs, both scoring sides, out-of-sample log-likelihood per row

run_dispersion.runline_side_note: criterion 2's estimand. `home` is the log loss on home margin >= 2 (home -1.5, equivalently away +1.5), `away` the log loss on home margin <= -2 (away -1.5, equivalently home +1.5), `both` their per-game sum. The board publishes all four prices and they are these two events; V1 of the pre-registration named no side and the first run scored `home` alone. See betting_model.RUNLINE_SIDE_AMENDMENT
run_dispersion.mode_note: forward split on season-to-date features. Both arms see the identical features and the identical fit window, so the contamination cannot favour one distribution over the other; this gate asks about SHAPE, not about skill

sensitivity.rule: the amended criterion 2 must pass at EVERY split quantile, with the other three criteria, or the gate is INDETERMINATE and dispersion stays off; a verdict that moves with the split point is a verdict about the split point
sensitivity.note: side-by-split sensitivity for the section 11a gate. `home` was the only reading the first run reported and V1 of the pre-registration did not name a side

run_dispersion.verdict_note: `passed` is the pre-registered single split under the amended criterion 2. `verdict` is the ship decision and comes from `sensitivity`, which requires that criterion to hold at every split quantile. Where they disagree, `verdict` governs and `served` follows it

vintage.note: 456 games graded on vintage features; 600 are needed before min_edge may be fitted, and the paired-Brier gate must also clear. 11 of the eval games carry no park term at all (their vintage predates the park column); the park index is NOT borrowed from the live file, which would leak the in-progress season

skill_vs_home_base.note: paired per-game Brier difference against the constant home-field baseline; positive means the model is better, and t >= 1.645 is the one-sided 95% bar

prob_calibration.criteria: fit (a, b) of p' = sigmoid(a*logit(p) + b) by MLE on the fit half only; on the held-out half BOTH must hold: (1) paired per-game Brier delta, identity minus Platt, > 0 at one-sided t >= 1.645; (2) paired log loss delta not worse on the point estimate (>= 0). Splits at date quantiles 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, ALL THREE or nothing, fit half >= 100 games and eval half >= 50 or the split cannot pass. Arm 1 is the vintage-gradable sample with {coefficients, tie, diff_shrink, home_adj} refit on each fit half; arm 2 is the calibration ledger's settled canonical-side moneyline games, ACTIVE only at n >= 100, same splits and criteria in settled order. Ship requires BOTH arms; serving is moneyline only.
prob_calibration.expectation: pre-registered: Platt repairs response scale, cannot manufacture discrimination, and is not expected to open the skill gate; converging toward the constant baseline is a finding. diff_shrink already absorbs most of the response scale, so a near-identity (a, b) is the honest likely outcome
prob_calibration.serving_scope: moneyline only; the runline and the total stay behind the dispersion gate (section 11a) whatever this block says

vintage_arm.note: features dated strictly before each game; the model is refit on each fit half, so nothing later than a split reaches either half

ledger_arm.basis: settled canonical-side moneyline games, one per game, from tools/betting_calibration; the model probabilities are the SERVED ones, priced from season-to-date inputs, which is exactly the scale the serve seam would apply to

prob_calibration.rule: both arms must pass, each at ALL THREE split quantiles, or the flag stays off; a green vintage arm alone is recorded, never served

benchmarks.claim_rule: never claim an unmeasured tier: a tier with n = 0 has no number and no claim, and a tier whose n is below the window's n is a SUBSAMPLE comparable only against the other tiers recomputed on those same games (its same_games block). The subsample is never the headline
benchmarks.surface: validation ladder only, dark: no slot, no record row and no exported edge reads a tier

model_vintage.source: the vintage block's own graded eval window

home_constant.source: the eval window's home win rate as a constant, the identical base brier_home_base uses

config.standing: literature priors, never fitted on the eval window or anywhere else; season starts flat, no carryover

elo_literature.source: tools/betting_elo.py walking this season's results only

same_games.note: the only comparison a subsample may appear in: every tier recomputed on exactly these games

market_open_devig.subsample_note: 223 of the window's 456 games have a cached open capture; a doubleheader's two games read the same capture
market_open_devig.source: proportional de-vig of the earliest open snapshot per slate, home fair probability averaged across books posting a two-sided h2h market

market_close_devig.status: no close capture matched a graded eval game; this tier is unmeasured and claims nothing. It auto-appears as close captures accrue; the close job runbook is section 3

min_edge_gate.min_edge_reduction: max over the tags that cleared; a floor above a tag's own measured threshold is stricter than that tag's evidence requires and can never be looser

gates.why: the contaminated forward margin over the home-field baseline is +0.005794 Brier with a paired sd of 0.08647, so a margin that size needs 603 games to clear one-sided 95%; 600 is that number, and a clean margin will be smaller, so this is a floor and not a pass

gates.need: paired Brier vs the home-field baseline, t >= 1.645
gates.why: sample size is not evidence; the model has to actually beat 'always take the home team' on games it could not see

gates.need: settled bets with a taken price, enough that some edge threshold clears an ROI lower bound of zero on at least 100 of them, WITHIN ONE TAG

board_all.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

ev_rank.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

longshot.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

potd_band.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

gates.why: an edge threshold is a claim about EV against real prices; 20 dates of odds snapshots are cached. The sweep runs per tag and a tag opens only if it individually clears - a pooled ROI measures a mixture nobody bet
gates.pooled_is_not_sweepable: `have` is the union of every tag and is never swept; see by_tag for the four clocks that are

sweep.reason: no tag cleared: 4 tag(s) present and none of them produced an ROI lower bound above zero on 100+ of its own settled rows

board_all.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

ev_rank.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

longshot.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

potd_band.reason: no edge threshold produced an ROI whose one-sided 95% lower bound clears zero on the graded sample

min_edge_gate.policy: min_edge stays null until all three gates are open. A threshold invented to make a pick appear is the single most dishonest number this module could publish.

note: Two modes, both labelled. The in-sample and forward numbers are CONTAMINATED: their features are season-to-date leaderboards that contain the games being graded. The vintage number is the honest one and it graded 456 games. A pick threshold is set from the vintage mode or from nothing.
